how_i_measured.test_suite: I ran `flutter test` three times from app/. With --reporter json: 75 suites loaded, 353 testDone events, 0 non-success, 1 skipped. With --reporter expanded the run reports `+225 ~1: All tests passed!` in 61 s — the expanded reporter compresses and names only 51 of the 75 files, which briefly looked like 25 suites silently not running; the json reporter shows every suite loads. I report the json numbers.
how_i_measured.boundary_probe: I wrote a throwaway lib/zz_probe_boundary.dart with four shapes of directive at once and ran test/persistence_boundary_test.dart against it, then deleted it.
how_i_measured.sixth_module_probe: I added a sixth module (lib/modules/plants/, two files), one import and one list entry in lib/modules/registry.dart, one EventTypeSpec in lib/spine/types.dart and one row in docs/EVENT_TYPES.md, ran the whole suite, then restored the tree (`git status --porcelain -- app docs` is empty).
how_i_measured.secret_scan: git rev-list --objects --all gave 8,994 objects; 4,727 have a text-ish path; I read every one of those blobs with git cat-file --batch and grepped for tskey-, BEGIN <...> PRIVATE KEY, assigned TS_AUTHKEY, and assigned store/key passwords. I read blob contents only — no commit messages, no log.
how_i_measured.assets: python3 tools/check/manifest.py, plus my own walk of assets/ against assets/MANIFEST.json in python.

rules.rule: 1. One event log and no second store; a file outside app/lib/spine/ that imports a storage driver fails the build.
rules.evidence: app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:15-19 looks for the URI anywhere in the directive up to its semicolon, over thirteen driver packages (:26-28) plus dart:indexed_db, dart:html, dart:js_interop and package:web when the file also names indexedDB/IDBFactory/IDBDatabase/localStorage/sessionStorage/openDatabase/caches (:49-53). I measured it rather than read it: a probe file carrying (a) a three-branch conditional import ending in package:sqlite3, (b) a double-quoted `export "package:hive/hive.dart"`, (c) an import of package:sembast broken over three lines with a `show` clause, and (d) package:web plus window.localStorage was caught on two of the three tests, naming lib/zz_probe_boundary.dart. Only lib/spine/store/*.dart import a driver in the real tree (store_sqlite.dart:10, store_web.dart:4). The hole: the rule enumerates packages and browser APIs and knows nothing about dart:io. A second probe holding a whole second event log — File('/tmp/second_spine.jsonl'), writeAsString of jsonEncoded events, a reader that parses them back — passed all three tests clean, `00:00 +3: All tests passed!`. And one file already writes outside the boundary under that exemption: app/lib/media/local_uri_io.dart:20-29 creates <tmp>/media/<hash>.<ext> and writes bytes to it. That one is benign (the bytes are already in the spine's own blob table, app/lib/spine/store/store.dart:31-35, and it exists so a platform player can be handed a file URI), but the guard cannot tell it from a real second store, which is what the rule is for.

rules.rule: 2. At least fourteen event types, docs/EVENT_TYPES.md and the code agreeing, each with a thread rendering, a notification treatment and a search behaviour, and a test asserting the same list.
rules.evidence: Eighteen types, app/lib/spine/types.dart:125-342, against a floor of fourteen. The id list is asserted both ways: app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:10-17 parses the numbered rows out of the document and `expect(documented, registered)`. Renderings: app/test/thread_types_test.dart:16-30 asserts every type names a renderer that exists in kThreadRenderers and every renderer is named by a type. Search: app/test/the_table_says_what_the_code_does_test.dart:66-99 asserts the excluded column, every text field the search column names, and the media facet. What is not asserted is the notification column — the table test parses it into the row map at :30 and no test in the file ever reads it back, and the thread-rendering column (cells[4]) is not even captured. The one place it has already drifted: docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:46 says milestone is 'on the day, interruptive, via a `ping` scheduled by a person' while app/lib/spine/types.dart:288 says `notify: Notify.quiet`. The nearest thing to a check is app/test/floors_test.dart:113, `expect(Notify.values.contains(spec.notify), isTrue)`, which is a tautology: `notify` is a non-nullable `Notify` (types.dart:62), so no value can fail it. That is the same vacuity the file's own comment at floors_test.dart:105-106 says it replaced ('used to assert that a non-nullable List was not null'), one line further down. Separately, the table test's :84 skips feeling_id and signal with the comment 'handled by name, below'; there is no below — the file ends at :99 — but the behaviour it was meant to cover is in fact implemented, at app/lib/spine/search.dart:96-114 (feeling id, name and family indexed for feeling and reaction) and :115 (signal for state_declared).

rules.rule: 3. A fifth shared-life module is a directory plus one line; the commit that added the fourth touched nothing under the first three.
rules.evidence: Five modules, app/lib/modules/registry.dart:10-16. app/test/module_costs_test.dart:35-75 is a real counting test: for every module it forbids the module's id, each of its event types, and each renderer the registry names for those types, as a quoted literal in any .dart under lib/ or any .js/.json/.html under web/, outside that module's own directory and lib/spine/types.dart. I measured the claim by building a sixth module — app/lib/modules/plants/{plants_module.dart,thread_row.dart}, one import and one entry in registry.dart, one EventTypeSpec in spine/types.dart, one row in docs/EVENT_TYPES.md. Nothing under the existing five had to change and module_costs_test, thread_types_test and spine_schema_test all passed. One shared file did have to change and it is not in any recipe: app/test/floors_test.dart:125-133 holds a closed hand-written list of the eighteen type ids and asserts `expect(unnamed, isEmpty)` against the registry, so the suite failed with 'the registry holds 19 types and this list names 18; these are not named: [plant_watered]'. The three-step recipe at docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:72-88 does not mention it, and neither does the cost accounting at app/lib/modules/module.dart:6-26, which says the spine registry 'is now the whole cost'. Two other failures in that run were my stub's fault and I say so: my build() returned a bare Column instead of ctx.fit(), which every_module_is_on_the_desk_test.dart:165 catches ('Expected: <6> Actual: <5>, one FitRows per module'), and my invented rowHeight of 53.0 against a measured 20.0, which a_module_knows_what_a_row_costs_test catches ('plants says a row costs 53.0 against a tallest of 20.0'). Both are the module contract working. The commit half of this rule I did not check: I have no build history and am not permitted to read the log, so I checked the structural claim by construction instead.

rules.rule: 4. Typing and presence ticks are never events; they must not reach the log.
rules.evidence: Ephemeral is a separate wire type with no path into the store: app/lib/transport/transport.dart:131-146. On the host they are held in a bounded in-memory list and drained into the pull response (app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:98-101, :283-289); on the client they land in AppScope._onEphemeral, which sets a flag and a six-second timer (app/lib/scope.dart:148-165) and never calls emit. The only writer is AppScope.emit → Spine.append (scope.dart:167-168), and Spine.append starts with specOf(type) (app/lib/spine/spine.dart:220), which throws ArgumentError on any id not in kEventTypes (types.dart:346-350) — 'typing' and 'presence' are not. Asserted rather than assumed: app/test/transport_local_test.dart:287-301 sends a typing frame client→host and a presence frame host→client, checks both arrive, and then checks both spines: `expect(r.host.length, 0); expect(r.client.length, 0)`.

rules.rule: 5. Read markers are never rendered as rows in the thread.
rules.evidence: Two independent guards. The projection returns before it can add a row: app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:320-326 handles read_marker by moving _readUpto and returning, and :327 returns for anything whose spec says !rowInThread. The registry says so at app/lib/spine/types.dart:216-226 (rowInThread: false, renderer 'ink_dries'), and 'ink_dries' maps to _neverARow at app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:175. Asserted at app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:31-34 and app/test/thread_types_test.dart:112-120.

rules.rule: 6. No secret in any committed file — working tree and history.
rules.evidence: Working tree: `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -n -I -E 'TS_AUTHKEY|tskey-'` returns only the variable's name in prose (README.md:23, bootstrap.sh:12/217/221, tools/tailscale/up.sh, app/test/reliability_test.dart:436-438) and never a value. History: 8,994 objects from git rev-list --objects --all, of which 4,727 have a text path; I read every one of those blobs and grepped for tskey-, BEGIN <...> PRIVATE KEY, an assigned TS_AUTHKEY, and assigned storePassword/keyPassword. Thirteen blobs matched and every one is a placeholder or a property name — 'TS_AUTHKEY=tskey-auth-… bash tools/tailscale/up.sh' in docs/PHONES.md, tools/tailscale/up.sh:4, app/test/reliability_test.dart, and `storePassword = key.getProperty("storePassword")` in app/android/app/build.gradle.kts. No path matching authkey|.jks|.keystore|key.properties|secret|.pem|.p12|id_rsa|.env was ever committed. .gitignore:12-15 covers .env, *.authkey and /toolchain/ts/; app/test/nothing_leaves_the_phone_test.dart:56-73 holds the android/.gitignore patterns and fails if key material appears under android/. Structurally there is nothing to store: the pairing key is derived from six spoken words and only the derived bytes are kept.

rules.rule: 7. The host binds only its tailnet address and refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key.
rules.evidence: The binding half is clean and well guarded. app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailnet.dart:22-33 admits only 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48; addressToServeOn (:56-71) refuses a declared address that is not one and throws NotOnTheTailnet rather than falling back when there is none; TailscaleBinding.hostBind (tailscale_transport.dart:72-79) is the only caller and there is no wildcard path through it. app/test/tailnet_test.dart:32-43 tries 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, 192.168.0.10 and :: as declared addresses and requires each to throw. The auth half is clean too: every /v1/ path except the two pairing calls goes through _refuseReason (server_io.dart:174-210) — header present, paired at all, the device this pairing covers, a timestamp inside kAuthSkew, a constant-time signature match, and a nonce not already spent on a non-GET — and a failure is 401 with the reason named. The static bundle is served unauthenticated by design, and insideTheBundle (:24-36) decides on the resolved path; app/test/the_bundle_server_stays_in_the_bundle_test.dart:51-63 throws fifteen hostile paths at it. What fails is the second clause of the story the build tells about this link. Neither HostBind construction ever passes a securityContext (tailscale_transport.dart:78, local_transport.dart:27), so server_io.dart:86-88 always takes the plain HttpServer.bind branch, and the client URL is built as 'http://' (tailscale_transport.dart:98-99; tailnet_test.dart:73 expects exactly 'http://[fd7a:115c:a1e0::9]:8443'). See the first two findings.

rules.rule: 8. Every file in assets/ has an entry in assets/MANIFEST.json naming its generator, and no asset or font came off the internet.
rules.evidence: 745 files under assets/; assets/MANIFEST.json has 742 entries and every one carries a non-empty `generator` (I checked all 742 in python: 0 without). The three unlisted are the manifests and index themselves — assets/MANIFEST.json, assets/sound/MANIFEST.sound.json, assets/tears/relief.json — which tools/check/manifest.py:22-23 exempts by name; `python3 tools/check/manifest.py` prints '740 files in assets/, 0 without an entry naming their generator' and exits 0. Ten generators account for everything, all of them in this repository: blender/folds/fold.py (240), blender/paper/tear_relief.py (168), blender/objects/objects.py (124), tools/tears/tear.py (57), blender/paper/stocks.py (54), blender/bits/bits.py (44), tools/sound/synth.py (44), tools/handwriting/build.py (7), tools/ink_plate.py (2), blender/shell/desk.py (2). The three fonts are among those seven: NoorHand.ttf, TeoHand.ttf and DeskStamp.ttf are built by tools/handwriting/build.py from tools/handwriting/{hands,skeletons}.json, whose sha256s are recorded in the entry for assets/fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json. A grep of tools/ and blender/ for urllib, requests, urlopen, wget, curl and http(s):// finds no fetch — every hit is a local variable named `curl` in a paper-deformation routine, a 127.0.0.1 capture URL, or apt-prereqs.sh installing system packages.

rules.rule: 9. The tests pass, and they test what they claim to.
rules.evidence: They pass: 75 suites, 353 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped, ~61 s (flutter test --reporter json, run twice with the same result). The skip is honest and is the best-handled thing in the suite: app/test/coldstart_test.dart:76-114 marks itself skipped rather than green when the two tailscaled nodes are not answering, and preserves the dated run in evidence/coldstart.json under `later_check` instead of overwriting it — which is what the file now says ('status': 'ran', written 2026-09-05, with a pending later_check dated 2026-09-11). I scanned every test body for one with no expect() and found none that survives inspection: the five my scanner flagged all assert through a helper (every_screen_builds_test.dart:57 `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)`, nothing_is_drawn_by_the_diagnostic_test.dart:87). Three assert less than their names. app/test/nothing_leaves_the_phone_test.dart:44-47 is called 'and nothing speaks cleartext' and comments 'The conversation is served over TLS to a tailnet address and nowhere else'; it asserts one attribute string in AndroidManifest.xml, and the app's only wire is plain HTTP. app/test/floors_test.dart:113 is a tautology on a non-nullable enum. app/test/the_table_says_what_the_code_does_test.dart:30 parses the notification column and never asserts on it.

findings.where: checklist.dart:72-76 and :119-123 (the 'certificate' step on both platforms), checklist.dart:204 (how it is observed), bootstrap_page.dart:19-100 (the iOS profile), tailscale_transport.dart:78 and :98-99 (what the transport actually does)
findings.what: The build carries two contradictory accounts of its own link: the transport is plain HTTP with no TLS anywhere (neither HostBind construction — tailscale_transport.dart:78, local_transport.dart:27 — ever passes a securityContext, so server_io.dart:86-88 always takes HttpServer.bind, and the client URL is built 'http://'), while the setup flow tells both people to trust a certificate — 'trust the certificate the other phone holds · so nothing between the two of you can read what goes across' on Android and 'install the profile the other phone is serving' on iPhone — and that step ticks itself on `link.state == LinkState.connected || link.state == LinkState.listening` (checklist.dart:204), which a host satisfies by listening, with no peer and no certificate in existence; the profile it points at is generated by mobileConfig()/bootstrapPage(), which have zero callers anywhere in lib/ and whose 'take the profile' link (/setup/profile.mobileconfig) nothing serves.
findings.why: Row 04 is coherence. checklist.dart:1-6 states the rule this breaks in its own words — 'Every step here ticks off a fact the app can see for itself: an address on the tailnet, a certificate that verified... Nothing ticks because someone pressed done, because a checklist that can be lied to is worse than none' — and this step ticks on a fact nobody observed, in a flow whose only instruction to an iPhone user leads to a page that does not exist. The build is not wrong to rely on WireGuard for confidentiality; tailscale_transport.dart:16-18 says so plainly. It is wrong to have shipped a second, louder account that contradicts it, and to have tested that account with app/test/nothing_leaves_the_phone_test.dart:44-47, whose name is 'and nothing speaks cleartext'.

findings.where: ambient_web.dart:82-96 (registration), against the address the PWA is actually served from, tailscale_transport.dart:98-99
findings.what: Because the host serves the bundle over http:// at a 100.64.0.0/10 address, the page the other phone loads is not a secure context, so navigator.serviceWorker is undefined; ambient_web.dart:82-83 returns silently on `container == null` and :93-96 swallows a failed register() into `_registration = null`. Every notification path then no-ops behind `if (!_allowed) return` / a null registration — the standing line (:110-126), the pocket knock (:133+) and everything web/push/sw.js does. Nothing in the evidence can see this, because evidence/logs/pwa.json was read at 'url': 'http://127.0.0.1:8798/', and 127.0.0.1 is the one http origin browsers treat as secure.
findings.why: The brief requires an Apple-compatible installable PWA and names a notification treatment for every event type; the registry carries a `pushed` word on thirteen of the eighteen (types.dart:135, :147, :161 …), Settings has a per-type interrupt row, and evidence/logs/webpush.txt proves the RFC 8291 record and the VAPID JWT are correct. All of it is unreachable on the only path the app ever serves the PWA over, and the capture proves it works on the one origin the app never uses.

findings.where: floors_test.dart:125-133, against the recipe at docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:72-88 and the cost accounting at app/lib/modules/module.dart:6-26
findings.what: A sixth shared-life module is not a directory plus one line. I built one and measured it: nothing under the existing five modules changed, and module_costs_test, thread_types_test and spine_schema_test were all green — but floors_test.dart holds a closed hand-written list of the eighteen type ids and asserts `expect(unnamed, isEmpty)` against the registry, so the suite failed with 'the registry holds 19 types and this list names 18; these are not named: [plant_watered]'. That shared test file is a fifth edit no document mentions: the recipe names three steps and module.dart:17 says the spine registry 'is now the whole cost'.
findings.why: Row 04 is extensibility, and the claim the row is measured against is exactly the one this falsifies. It is also the failure mode floors_test.dart:119-123 was rewritten to prevent — a hand-written list that 'agrees with the code on the day it is written and never again' — reintroduced in the direction the author did not check: the list is now kept honest about deletions and enforces itself against additions.

findings.where: persistence_boundary_test.dart:15-19 and :26-28, the enumerated driver list
findings.what: The rule that is supposed to fail the build for a second store is an enumeration of thirteen pub packages and four browser-storage entry points, and it knows nothing about dart:io. I put a whole second event log in lib/ — File('/tmp/second_spine.jsonl'), writeAsString of jsonEncoded events, a reader that parses them back, no package import at all — and all three tests passed ('00:00 +3: All tests passed!'). In the same run the four adversarial directive shapes I tried (a three-branch conditional import, a double-quoted export, a multi-line import with a show clause, package:web plus localStorage) were all caught, so the enumeration itself is well built. One file already writes outside the boundary through the gap: app/lib/media/local_uri_io.dart:20-29.
findings.why: 'One event log and no second store' is the build's first named structural failure condition, and the guard that is supposed to make it unfalsifiable is falsifiable by the simplest second store there is. The existing offender is harmless — it caches blob bytes that are already in the spine's blob table so a platform player can be handed a file URI — but the rule cannot distinguish it from a real one, which is the whole point of having the rule rather than a convention.

findings.where: the_table_says_what_the_code_does_test.dart:30 and :35-99; floors_test.dart:113; the live disagreement at docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:46 vs app/lib/spine/types.dart:288
findings.what: Of the three per-type properties rule 2 names, the notification treatment is the one nothing checks. The table test parses the notification column into its row map at :30 and no test in the file reads it back; the thread-rendering column is not captured at all; and the only assertion on Notify anywhere is floors_test.dart:113, `expect(Notify.values.contains(spec.notify), isTrue)`, which cannot fail because `notify` is a non-nullable enum (types.dart:62). It has already drifted once: docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:46 says milestone is 'on the day, interruptive' and types.dart:288 says Notify.quiet.
findings.why: The whole file exists, by its own header at :1-8, so that the next drift in that table is found by the build rather than by a reader with an afternoon; one of the four columns it reads is still read by a person only. And floors_test.dart:105-106 says in its own comment that this test 'used to assert that a non-nullable List was not null, which is to say it asserted nothing at all' — the same shape survives seven lines later.

findings.what: Fourteen of the seventeen artifacts are present and all fourteen are from_this_run with meets_minimum true — nothing in the set is a still of an older build. Three are missing. 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png are environmental and the reason is measured rather than asserted ('adbd answered after 113 minutes and the framework never came up behind it', no /dev/kvm, no GTK, and neither was faked from the PWA), which I accept. 15_authored_feeling.mp4 is a real failure of the build's own gate: evidence/frames.json records repeated_frames 1 at frame 74 and one brightness jump, ok false, 'the brief allows none', and the manifest correctly refuses to count the earlier copy still on disk.
findings.why: Only one of the three is the app's fault and the record says which, at the right level of specificity, with the run that failed named rather than the artifact quietly absent. I record it as a finding because a missing artifact is one, not because the reason is evasive — it is not.

what_is_working: The single spine is real and the boundary around it is real for every way a driver is normally reached. Only app/lib/spine/store/store_sqlite.dart:10 and store_web.dart:4 import one; the rule at persistence_boundary_test.dart:15-19 caught all four adversarial directive shapes I threw at it, including the conditional import the comment says a previous critic got through.

Eighteen event types against a floor of fourteen, with the id list asserted in both directions against the document (spine_schema_test.dart:10-17) and the rendering asserted in both directions against the code (thread_types_test.dart:16-30 — every type names a renderer that exists, every renderer is named by a type).

There is one sentence per event, not two. summaryOf (renderers.dart:~205-240) is what search, notifications and the thread's margin line all read, module_costs_test.dart:99-127 asserts a module's own sentence and summaryOf agree, and thread_types_test.dart:70-88 forbids an ISO timestamp or an underscored payload key ever reaching a person — with a fixture ('warm_palm') chosen to be the shape that used to slip through.

module_costs_test.dart:35-75 is the strongest test in the suite: it forbids not just a module's event type but the renderer id the registry names for it and the module's own id, as a quoted literal, in any .dart under lib/ or any .js/.json/.html under web/, outside that module's directory. Building a sixth module confirmed it: nothing under the existing five had to change.

Ephemeral frames have no path into the log — separate wire type, bounded in-memory queue, and Spine.append would throw on the id anyway — and transport_local_test.dart:287-301 checks both spines are length 0 after sending one in each direction rather than only that the frame arrived.
The tailnet binding is one function with no wildcard path through it, and tailnet_test.dart:32-43 tries the four addresses a mistake would reach for and requires each to throw rather than bind.
745 assets, 742 manifest entries, zero without a named generator, ten generators all in this repository, three synthesised fonts, and no network fetch anywhere in tools/ or blender/.
No secret has ever been committed: 8,994 objects scanned, 13 pattern hits, every one a placeholder with an ellipsis or a property name.

The one skipped test is the right kind of skip. coldstart_test.dart:95-102 says in its own comment why a test that returns before any expect() is a lie to the reader, calls markTestSkipped, and preserves the dated run in evidence/coldstart.json rather than overwriting it with a pending line.
verdict: The architecture this row is about is genuinely good, and unusually, it is good in a way I could measure rather than take on trust: one spine with one store behind a boundary that caught every adversarial import I wrote, eighteen event types with the document held to the code in both directions, one sentence per event that search and a lock screen and the thread all read, and a module-cost test strict enough that building a sixth module really did leave the other five untouched. Three things keep it below thirteen. The blocking one is that the build carries two contradictory accounts of its own link: the transport is plain HTTP with no TLS construction anywhere, while the setup checklist instructs both people to trust a certificate, ticks that step on a socket being open, and points an iPhone at a configuration profile generated by a function with no callers and served at a path nothing serves — in a file whose own first paragraph says a checklist that can be lied to is worse than none. That is not a quibble about WireGuard, which does carry the confidentiality the transport file correctly claims; it is a second, louder story about the same link that the code does not implement, that a test with the name 'nothing speaks cleartext' certifies off a manifest attribute, and that has one concrete consequence nobody can see in the evidence: the PWA is served from an http:// tailnet address, which is not a secure context, so the service worker never registers and the whole notification apparatus — proven correct in webpush.txt, wired through every registry entry's `pushed` word — is dead on the only path the app uses, while evidence/logs/pwa.json shows it working at 127.0.0.1, the one http origin where it would. The other two are smaller and both are the row's own promises: a sixth module is a directory plus one line plus a hand-written list in app/test/floors_test.dart that no recipe mentions, and the rule that forbids a second store is an enumeration of packages that a second store written with dart:io walks straight past. Fix the certificate story — either build the TLS the checklist describes or delete the step, the profile page and the test that certifies it, and say plainly that the tailnet is the encryption — and this row is comfortably over its floor.
opened: docs/EVENT_TYPES.md — read under the no-docs rule because rule 2 names this one file and cannot be checked without it; I opened nothing else in docs/

not_worth_opening.what: the seventeen artifacts themselves (01_pulse.png … 17_setup_pwa.png) and evidence/crops/

not_worth_opening.what: evidence/DIFF.json, evidence/reliability.json, evidence/logs/*.report.json, the per-scene logs and fling logs
not_worth_opening.why: They measure what the running app did, which the messenger and emotional-transmission rows are scored on. The framing of each shot. Useful for telling a fault in the app from a fault in how the picture was taken, which is a question about artifacts I am not scoring.
